image:image.image:title: British warning sign at Kibbutz Ruhama, 1946
image:image.image:caption: "Disperse at once - otherwise we will open fire", in Hebrew and Arabic. Posted at the besieged settlement during the British weapons search of August 1946.

image:image.image:title: A young woman beside the British warning sign, Ruhama 1946
image:image.image:caption: The only photograph in the collection in which a person and the military authority appear in the same frame.

image:image.image:title: The yard at Kibbutz Ruhama after the search, 1946
image:image.image:caption: Machinery, beams, crates and tools heaped together after six days of searching. One of the members stands at the left.

image:image.image:title: Smashed dining-hall crockery, Kibbutz Ruhama 1946
image:image.image:caption: Thousands of plates and cups from the communal dining hall, broken and thrown into a single heap.

image:image.image:title: A woman in the wrecked kitchen, Ruhama 1946
image:image.image:caption: Not a picture of destruction but of repair - someone has started putting the kitchen back together.

image:image.image:title: A member of Kibbutz Ruhama standing among the wreckage, 1946
image:image.image:caption: His name is not known. Someone alive today may recognise him.

image:image.image:title: Floor and wall broken open during the search, Ruhama 1946
image:image.image:caption: Paving smashed and the ground beneath dug out, looking for an arms cache that was not there.

image:image.image:title: A slit mattress, Ruhama 1946
image:image.image:caption: Every mattress in the kibbutz was cut open and emptied during the six-day search.
